title: Unified failure profiles map and tracehook sample-rate governor
creator: Aisha Gupta
description:
Goal: Build a single, queryable dashboard that maps runtime failures across the inference stack (network timeouts, queue overload, model runtime errors, invalid model outputs, HTTP/gRPC codes) and implement a low-latency tracehook sample-rate governor to ensure high-fidelity traces for problematic slices without saturating storage/ingest costs.

Background: We have many point dashboards and ad-hoc trace sampling knobs. When a customer reports higher error-rate the oncall or SRE handoffs currently chase disparate metrics (latency percentiles in runtime, grpc status distribution in ingress, model inference errors emitted by model adapters). This ticket unifies taxonomy, centralizes visualization, and adds a smart sampling mechanism so traces are available for root-cause and postmortems while keeping cost predictable.

Scope:
- Define canonical failure taxonomy values and mappings from spans/logs/metrics: client_timeout, server_timeout, overload_dropped, overload_queue_delay, model_runtime_error, model_output_schema_error, http_4xx, http_5xx, grpc_unavailable, grpc_cancelled, grpc_deadline_exceeded.
- Instrument tracehooks to attach failure_tag and failure_code to the request span at the earliest detection point.
- Implement a sample-rate governor service that:
  * applies higher sampling to requests that hit any failure_tag or cross configured percentiles (p95> threshold)
  * supports a budgeted background sampling rate for healthy traffic to maintain baselines
  * exposes runtime knobs per tenant/route/model in config (console + flag).
- Create Grafana/Console dashboard panels showing: failure profile distribution over time, failure taxonomy heatmap by route/model/region, trace link column for the top error slices, SLI exposure by failure type, and cost delta estimator for enabling higher sampling on a route.
- Add metrics/log pipeline rules to normalize failure_code labels and enrich logs with model_version and routing_bucket.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Dashboard exists in Console -> Observability -> Failure Profiles and shows failure breakdown with filters for model, route, region, and deployment (hosted/dedicated/private).
2) Each failure row includes a direct trace link when sampled; sampled traces for failures should be available for at least 95% of unique failure_id events during a 24h window for flagged routes.
3) Sample-rate governor can be toggled per-route and provides a projected ingest cost delta.
4) Failure taxonomy mappings are published in Confluence and used by the metrics pipeline to produce normalized metric tags (failure.taxonomy).
5) Unit and e2e tests added for sampling logic and tracehook enrichment; integration test validates that a synthetic overload event produces the expected failure tag and a sampled trace link appears on the dashboard.

Non-goals: auto-remediation, auto-rollbacks, or complex ML-based anomaly classification (this ticket aims to provide the observable surface and deterministic sampling).
tasks: Define taxonomy and publish mapping doc in Confluence: /confluence/display/OBS/Failure+Profiles+Taxonomy
Tracehook: add failure_tag and failure_code span attributes; update runtime SDKs
Sampling service: implement governor with budget and route knobs; add feature flag
Metrics pipeline: add normalization rule and enrich logs with model_version and routing_bucket
Dashboards: new panels in Grafana and Console + cost estimator widget
Tests: unit tests for governor, integration test with synthetic overload scenario
Docs: Confluence doc + short runbook for oncall
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: increased trace ingress cost if sampling misconfigured -> Mitigation: governor enforces global budget and provides projected cost before enabling per-route override
Risk: inconsistent taxonomy across services -> Mitigation: add small adapter layer in metrics pipeline to normalize legacy labels, require rollout to be gated by integration tests
Risk: missed failure attribution when model adapter swallows errors -> Mitigation: add assertion checks and a lightweight span assertion library in model adapters
success_metrics: Dashboard adoption: oncall uses Failure Profiles during 90% of incidents involving inference errors for 30 days after GA
Trace coverage: >=95% sampled traces available for unique failure_id events on flagged routes
Reduction in TTR: median time-to-resolution for inference error incidents reduced by 25% on routes with sampling enabled
review_feedback: PM Sofia Martinez: prefer conservative default sampling budget and explicit opt-in for enterprise tenants
Design Alex Park: keep dashboard UI compact; prioritize table-first view with quick filters
SRE Jamie Li: require toggle in console that can be used during incidents to raise sample rate temporarily without a deploy
implementation_notes: Prototype of the governor was implemented in a feature branch (/observability/features/sampling-governor). Performance measurement shows CPU overhead <1% at 10k QPS. We need infra approval for a small Redis-backed token bucket to persist budgets across runtime instances. Will reuse existing tracehook registration points in runtime agent. Work staged as three PRs: tracehook enrichment, sampling service, dashboard wiring.
